title: Absit nomen!
html_source:
Another example of a harmless expression that contains rather complex wordplay. First of all, absit nomen! (literally “let the name be absent”) is a play on absit omen, which is is the Latin equivalent of “Knock on wood!”. Stephen is obviously referring to some ominous meaning of the name “Myrto”. What could it be?

“Myrto” is derived from the Greek Μυρτε, which translates to “myrtle”. It is the name of a plant used to adorn brides in wedding ceremonies. Thus, “myrtle” has become associated with virginity.

In other words, when Stephen is saying “Myrto (absit nomen!)” he is actually making a dirty joke.
